name: Simple flat-priced live-quiz tool for teachers and small trainers
buyer: Individual teacher, tutor or small-business trainer who pays personally or from a small budget
pain: Free-tier player caps (Kahoot's free plan allows 10 players per game, 3 on a business signup), confusing plans, and billing and cancellation complaints.
wedge: A live-quiz game with no player accounts, a free tier at 100 players, one-click cancellation and a flat $5/month or $29/year plan. The notes call it weak because free alternatives already exist and a solo entrant has no teacher distribution.

scan1Edge.entrant_basis: Flat $5/month tier with near-zero marginal cost for a software-only product. This is a price edge only, and the notes' 85-90% saving depends on which Kahoot price is correct.
scan1Edge.falsifier: Blooket and Trivia Anywhere already offer free tiers (C31), so if teachers take free alternatives or Kahoot's $3 entry plan, the paid price gives no edge.
scan1Edge.unit: USD per month for a paid teacher plan

substitutesNoted.name: Kahoot
substitutesNoted.price_point: Free (capped); teacher plans $3-$19/mo billed yearly; business $19-$79 per licence/mo

unitEconomicsNoted.notes: Model: $5/month (or $29/year) with ~85% margin per the owner's estimate. Revenue per user is low and seasonal.

majorUncertainty: Whether teachers will pay when Blooket, Trivia Anywhere and Kahoot's free tier exist, and whether a solo founder can reach teachers at all.
unknowns: Kahoot pricing is inconsistent across sources
Trivia Anywhere's 'no limits' claim is unverified
Compliance cost for student data laws
Whether Kahoot's reported billing complaints translate into switching
regulatoryOrPlatformDependency: Student data laws (FERPA, COPPA, state laws) apply if minors use the product. School procurement is slow.
